coordination_failures: Critical shortage of repair crews led to mission failures in infrastructure (m13 failed, m12 delayed).
Resource utilization reported as 0.0 despite high demand—suggests misallocation or tracking error.
High rejection rate for road repair requests (14 rejections) hampered access to disaster zones.
headline: Overwhelmed Infrastructure Response Leads to High Casualties Despite Early Medical Success

key_moments.description: Four high-severity missions launched simultaneously, straining initial response capacity.
Second wave of missions began; medical_surge in old_town failed due to resource exhaustion.
Third wave of severe incidents overwhelmed system; two infra repairs failed or incurred heavy losses.
Mission m13 officially failed—repair crew shortages culminated in 12 preventable deaths.

lessons: Pre-position repair crews before cascading infrastructure failures occur.
Balance early medical/fire response with sustained infrastructure support.
Track and report actual resource usage to avoid misleading utilization metrics.
Prioritize road repair access to enable timely response across all sectors.
Avoid overcommitting resources in initial wave—reserve capacity for later surges.
what_worked: Early medical and fire missions (t0–t8) were resolved efficiently with high lives saved.
All missions were eventually closed—none remained open at simulation end.
Low panic level (0.08) indicates effective public communication or crowd control.
